states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control. Because the timing of his Monday-night apixaban dose is uncertain, Dr. Patel is changing the approach from direct cardioversion to TEE-guided cardioversion so a clot can be checked for first while still avoiding an unnecessary delay. The Wednesday, March 11 slot was released; the new tentative procedure slot is Thursday, March 12 at 11:10 AM with 9:40 AM arrival, and that Thursday slot is now specifically a TEE-guided cardioversion case. Scheduler Terry has updated the arrival letter in the portal, and Marcus's own portal copy prep line now says TEE-guided cardioversion. Marcus requests that the procedure slot details be put in the chart. Dr. Patel has reviewed the labs and stated they are acceptable for outpatient cardioversion, satisfying the pending-labs condition; full medication history reconciliation remains part of the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion, and to continue apixaban exactly as prescribed without missing any further doses. Pharmacist Klein confirms apixaban stays at 5 mg twice daily and Marcus must not stop or skip it on his own unless the cardiologist specifically says otherwise. The only routine periprocedural hold discussed is lisinopril on the morning of the procedure once the date is confirmed. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active.

states.content: Marcus Reed permits use of his cell phone and the patient portal for routine contact, and says the backup line is only for failed reach attempts. His primary contact is his regular cell 617-555-0104, and he asks that any result callbacks use his cell first unless that fails. He asks that the Cedar Bridge number not be called unless his cell fails. He does not want his cell number used if someone needs to discuss the procedure or his heart rhythm. Backup contact details are not needed unless cardiology requests them. Messages should use generic callback wording only, asking them to have Marcus call Riverside Cardiology back, and must not mention cardioversion, atrial fibrillation, blood thinner, or recovery housing. Routine reminders should go to the patient portal whenever possible. Marcus is fine with the portal wording saying TEE-guided cardioversion, but does not want that wording used in family or voicemail messages.

Medication changes, lab results, adherence history, and chart notes must not be shared with her. For the tentative Wednesday cardioversion slot, Nina is to be told only the Wednesday time and arrival window, with nothing about the medication plan. Marcus does not want details of his recovery discussed with family; family updates should be limited to the logistics scope he set, and nurse Jamison has agreed to keep family updates within that scope. Marcus wants his sister told the times later, but not the reason anything changes. Nurse Elise confirmed that telling Nina the new arrival time without the reason falls within the logistics-only scope through Monday, and she will leave the reason out; she can confirm the updated arrival time only when Marcus permits it and cannot discuss medication adherence or clinical reasons for the schedule change. Marcus explicitly does not want anyone telling Nina that the apixaban dose-timing matter came up. The TEE-guided cardioversion wording is acceptable in Marcus's portal copy but must not be used in family or voicemail messages.
